problems.title: Control feature sizes match only a restricted resolution class
problems.source_location: Eqs. (5)–(6), PDF pp. 5–6; author cunet_arch.py, lines 96–165; inference entry, line 123.
claim: The inference tool accepts RAW images and relies on model padding/cropping, but its control branch adds a fixed two rows before alignment.
analysis: The backbone addition uses size \((4\lceil H/16\rceil,4\lceil W/16\rceil)\), while the control branch uses \((\lfloor H/4\rfloor+2,\lfloor W/4\rfloor)\). At \(H=W=32\), these are \(8\times8\) and \(10\times8\). Compatibility requires \(H\bmod16\in\{8,9,10,11\}\) and \(W\bmod16=0\). The paper's packed camera shape \(2344\times3520\) satisfies the condition, so the witness does not refute that default geometry.
result: The code arithmetic proves an input-domain defect without running a model. It does not show failure at the original camera geometry.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Align control size to the padded backbone feature shape, or state the restricted input domain. No end-to-end corrected model result is asserted.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The released training path omits zero residual initialization
problems.source_location: Text following Eq. (6), PDF p. 6; author cunet_arch.py, lines 8–11 and 28–40; stage-two training configuration.
claim: The method describes zero-initialized convolutional residual blocks.
analysis: The zero_module helper is defined but the four ResidualBlock instances construct default Conv2d layers without invoking it. A fresh stage-two network has no pretrained network_g in the traced configuration, so loading the ratio estimator cannot initialize these residual branches to zero.
result: A specific release/training-recipe discrepancy is supported. Nonzero trained weights alone would not be evidence, and the original historical training version remains unknown.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Initialize the residual branch as specified, or identify the historical initialization actually used. Zeroing its final convolution gives zero initial residual algebraically.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Requested \(16\)-bit pixel values wrap during final \(8\)-bit export
problems.source_location: Author UltraLED inference documentation; image_process_ultraled.py, lines 87–88 and 126–131.
claim: The script exposes output bit depth but always casts the returned array to uint8 before saving.
analysis: On the requested 16-bit path, valid values \[[0,255,256,32768,65535]\] cast to uint8 become \([0,255,0,0,255]\). This is modular truncation, not monotonic 16-to-8-bit rescaling. The cast occurs after selected-bit-depth postprocessing and before imwrite.
result: The nondefault 16-bit export path has a concrete encoding defect. Default 8-bit behavior and original evaluation scores are outside this counterexample.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Preserve uint16 for the 16-bit output path; explicitly rescale and label an 8-bit preview if desired.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
